summary: Forest Lookouts quotes an October 1960 newspaper report of a planned fire watch tower near Kosoma; no source confirms it was built or describes the site today.

events.note: Legislative appropriation for four fire watch towers, as described in the 1960 report.
Announced plan (October 1, 1960) for a new fire watch tower near Kosoma, Pushmataha County. A plan, not a completed tower.

evidence.supports: page titled for Flat Top Mountain
report attributed to The Daily Oklahoman
announced plans for a tower near Kosoma
evidence.quote: Jack Cornelius Jr., state board of agriculture president, Friday announced plans construction of a new fire watch tower near Kosoma in Pushmataha County.
The tower will be built with a 1959 legislative appropriation for four such towers to help safeguard southeastern Oklahoma timber land.

evidence.supports: 23 state fire towers at one time
evidence.quote: At one time, there were 23 state fire towers within the Oklahoma Forestry Services Fire Protection Area.
As fire tower observers have retired, they have been replaced by planes that fly over the area.

evidence.supports: three towers still staffed; remaining towers house radio repeaters
evidence.quote: Today there are only three fire towers still staffed with the remaining towers used to house radio repeaters

sources.title: History of the Oklahoma State Forestry Division

notes_for_editor: Only source for this site is the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes a Daily Oklahoman item (October 1, 1960) announcing a plan. Open question: whether the planned tower near Kosoma is the Flat Top Mountain site this record covers. The page is titled for Flat Top Mountain and names Pushmataha County, but neither source ties the page to Kosoma. Two WebSearch queries found no Flat Top tower in Pushmataha County. Next checks: Gateway to Oklahoma History (gateway.okhistory.org) for 1960-61 newspaper follow-ups, the Pushmataha Historical Society, and Oklahoma Forestry Services.
